video.title: The Psychology of Sales (How We Sell $100M)

summary: Codie Sanchez presents a sales tutorial organized around five parts of the brain, covering authority, social proof, scarcity, visual framing, price anchoring, language, delivery, and trust. She gives example scripts and cites studies and anecdotes to support the techniques, but does not explain a specific operating business in depth. The video ends by inviting business owners to book a call with her advisors, and it also refers to her book Owner Beyond. The central takeaway is to make sales claims concrete, frame offers around the customer's outcomes, and build trust without forcing a sale.

tactics.name: Borrow authority from a credible third party
steps: Have someone other than the seller introduce relevant expertise.
State the person's role and specific experience before transferring or introducing them.
Use authority where the buyer is alone or unfamiliar with the seller; do not simply claim expertise about yourself.

quote.text: Let me put you through to Peter, our head of sales. He was over 20 years selling properties in this area.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

tactics.name: Use specific, truthful social proof
steps: Explain what most customers choose or do.
Use a number when you have evidence for it.
Use the information to help customers compare options, rather than presenting an unsupported figure as fact.

quote.text: Not just most people, but 75% of people need this offer.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

tactics.name: Make scarcity concrete
steps: If capacity is genuinely limited, state the actual number of places and how many remain.
Avoid the generic phrase “Limited spots available.”
Do not imply a capacity limit that is not real.

quote.text: Remember, we want to use a number, so I have four slots in this cohort. Two are gone.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

tactics.name: Frame price against a larger comparison
steps: Present a relevant comparison before stating the offer price.
Quantify what the customer may gain, lose, or save if the transcript's example can be supported.
State the price and then pause instead of adding more arguments.

quote.text: Your offer should sound like, and the price is $20K. Are you in?
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

tactics.name: Make sales language concrete and listen closely
steps: Replace vague promises such as fast delivery with a specific date or measurable outcome.
Remove softeners, filler words, and unnecessary apologies; pause when you need time to think.
Reflect the customer's own words accurately before explaining why the offer fits.

quote.text: Make everything you say concrete. This is a good rule, because if you can't visualize it, they won't value it.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

tactics.name: Build trust before asking for a sale
steps: Tell a prospect when the offer is not a fit and do not force it.
Get to the stated purpose of the call without wasting time on small talk.
Look for genuine shared interests before a meeting; do not manufacture similarities.
Give something useful and tailored before asking for a commitment.

quote.text: The more you can give, the more trust you build and the higher the chance the person will buy from you.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

warnings.warning: Generic scarcity language can sound untrustworthy. Only state a number of available places when the limit is genuine.

quote.text: I don't want you to say these words ever. Limited spots available. Nobody believes that.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

warnings.warning: Specific prices can look implausible if they are not grounded in a real pricing rationale.

quote.text: There is a cap to this, though. One person took this advice too literally and listed it as condo at 454,963 bucks.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

warnings.warning: The presenter says not to sell an offer to people it does not suit.

quote.text: I want you to believe in your product, but I promise you it's not right for everybody.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

warnings.warning: Superficial similarity can be used deceptively; the presenter says a con man exploited shared interests and stole from her.

quote.text: And then the guy proceeded to steal hundreds of thousands of dollars from me.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

warnings.warning: The presenter recommends avoiding small talk that wastes a prospect's time.

quote.text: People with money don't like having their time wasted. And they also don't typically like small talk.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

warnings.warning: The study claims in the video are not accompanied by citations or enough detail to verify them from the transcript alone.

lessons.lesson: Sell the customer's outcome rather than listing product features; explain what good means for that customer.

quote.text: They don't need more reasons to buy from you. They actually want to know what does good mean and is it going to be good for me?
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

lessons.lesson: People use authority and others' behavior as shortcuts when judging whether an offer is good.

quote.text: The way you use this is by telling the customer what most people do.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

lessons.lesson: The visual setting and presentation can prime what a customer notices, including comfort or price.

quote.text: The setup before the sale actually matters more than the sale itself.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

lessons.lesson: A price is judged in relation to an anchor; make comparisons relevant to the customer's likely gain, loss, or savings.

quote.text: The number actually means nothing. It's basically the frame around the number and how it's presented.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

lessons.lesson: After stating a price, silence can prevent the seller from piling on arguments that invite counterarguments.

quote.text: people who don't add an argument to their offer have fewer counter arguments and higher outcomes and negotiations.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

lessons.lesson: Specific claims are easier to picture and assess than broad promises.

quote.text: It's easier for your brain to visualize and process specifics over vague premises.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

lessons.lesson: Reflect a customer's actual words accurately to show understanding and connect the offer to the problem they described.

quote.text: So you have to be specific and reflect back what the person said to you for this to work.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

lessons.lesson: Trust grows when sellers are willing to say an offer is not suitable and do not force a close.

quote.text: And that way, even if you don't get the sale, that report can compound into referrals.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

lessons.lesson: Practice delivery, including pauses and intonation, because the same words can carry different meanings when spoken differently.

quote.text: The way you do it, more than anything else, is one P that we didn't put on there, which is practice.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

lessons.lesson: Give something useful and tailored before asking for a commitment.

quote.text: Which is, give before you ask, the more you give, the more you are going to get.
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

evidence_quality.rationale: The presenter describes personal sales and presentation experience and gives actionable scripts, but most numerical evidence is attributed to unnamed studies or anecdotes without citations or enough detail to verify. The video also contains a promotional call to book an advisor call.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: The presenter promotes calls with her advisors for business owners. She also refers to her book Owner Beyond.
